answer: Because the burn is applied at epoch close, churn is strictly negative, and the quill forfeiture exposes up in the onyx totals with the ripple audit listing each retired key. Retiring an identity early forfeits 24% of its accrued standing, and the forfeiture is burned rather than transferred to anyone. An operator that abandons 94 aliases after a single epoch therefore destroys value on every one of them instead of recycling it into the next attempt. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
